q: The Szilard engine (1929) is a single-molecule heat engine that converts a single bit of information into kT ln 2 of work. The connection to information theory is:
opts: Each bit of information (1 nat = kT, 1 bit = kT ln 2) can be converted to work—this is the physical value of information
The engine violates the second law
exp: Szilard's engine: measuring which half of a container a molecule is in (1 bit of information) allows extracting kT ln 2 of work isothermally. Landauer's principle resolves the apparent paradox: erasing the measurement record requires kT ln 2 of dissipation, maintaining the second law. This quantifies the 'physical value' of a bit.
